Vlad and White revisit *American Me*, Edward James Olmos, the controversial Mexican Mafia rape scene, and Mendoza’s claims about Joe Morgan, his brother Angel, Kern County, and the Black Guerrilla Family. A stark look at prison gangs, survival, trauma, and the consequences of gang loyalty.

recentItems.description:

--------
Ramon “Mundo” Mendoza sits down with VladTV for an uncensored account of his path from Boyle Heights altar boy to Mexican Mafia member known as “Machine Gun Mundo.” Born in East Los Angeles in 1949, Mendoza details childhood violence, early gang life, juvenile hall, San Quentin, Folsom, and the prison politics behind La Eme, Nuestra Familia, Norteños and Sureños. He discusses his first killing involving White Fence member Robert Lopez, his relationship with Joe “Pegleg” Morgan, street and prison hits he says totaled more than two dozen, and later cooperation with law enforcement after a Christian conversion.

Mendoza also addresses Kern County cases, witness protection, threats tied to organized crime, and Hollywood portrayals of the Mexican Mafia in *American Me*, including Edward James Olmos, Danny Trejo, and the controversy surrounding the film. A rare firsthand interview on gangs, prison power, informants, redemption, and consequences.

In this candid conversation with Shawn Prez, former Army Ranger sniper Nicholas Irving answers a provocative hypothetical: with one shot anywhere in world history, he says he would try to stop the Romans who captured Yeshua/Jesus, standing with Peter despite the risk of altering destiny and faith itself. Irving reflects on whether the crucifixion was predestined, comparing the moment to Neo in *The Matrix* while wrestling with belief, violence, and redemption.

The discussion then turns deeply personal as Irving opens up about combat, PTSD, and the mindset shaped by Iraq, Afghanistan, 9/11, and elite military culture. He references Rob O’Neill, SEAL Team Six, Delta Force, Marine Recon, Army Rangers, Dahlonega, Georgia, and his own path from Maryland to war. Irving explains why, in combat, survival and protecting teammates mattered more than politics or “freedom,” offering a raw look at the cost of becoming a warrior.

--------
Former Mexican Mafia member Ramon “Mundo” Mendoza sits down with Vlad to discuss the brutal loyalty codes that ruled his life, including whether he would have carried out an order against his own brother, Angel. Mendoza recalls Joe Morgan attempting to sponsor Angel into the organization after a hit involving a Black Guerilla Family member, and explains why he blocked the move to spare their mother from heartbreak.

The conversation also covers Mendoza’s Kern County arrest, his time in Southern California awaiting U.S. Marshals protection, an ex-con with a gun charge, and why he still hides his face decades after leaving prison. Vlad connects Mendoza’s story to witness protection, Alpo Martinez of Harlem and Paid in Full, and the Tupac murder case in Las Vegas. Now 76, Mendoza speaks on faith, law enforcement training, redemption, and the lasting cost of gang life.
